atomic_cutover: Cut 1 removes the twelve keys that fall without a policy decision and without touching the fixture core 137 packages consume. internal/testdb derives clone names, template suffixes and cache keys with hash/fnv and math/rand/v2 instead of crypto/sha1, crypto/sha256 and crypto/rand; the unused crypto/sha1 classification leaves the policy. test/e2e/calendar mints tokens through the api/testutil claim builders TenantUserTestClaims and ParentTestClaims. test/e2e/timetable binds the kiosk actor through testutil.WithDeviceActor, resolves tenant contexts through testpkg.ContextForTenant, and reads the audit deletion type it asserts on as the stored string. Cut 2 (policy epoch 24, ADR 0039) grants the shared fixture owner its four standing targets — its own tooling, tenant-runtime/public, legacy-shared/domain and security-runtime/contract — through six shared-fixtures.* rules, removes the ten keys they resolve, and returns the calendar and timetable suites to the permission constants. No route, status code, error string, table or write owner changes. Cut 3 needs no rule: the fixture catalog maps the iot.devices, facilities.rooms, activities.categories/groups/student_enrollments/schedules/supervisors and schedule.* rows it writes and returns (test/device_rows.go, facility_rows.go, activity_rows.go, schedule_rows.go), the way #3556 mapped the School Structure rows; suites that hand a fixture row to an owner repository read it back through that repository or carry it field for field into the owner model in their own package. api/testutil binds the kiosk staff principal from IDs (WithStaffContext, WithDeviceActor; the unused StaffPrincipal is deleted) and re-exports the People Directory suite constructors from the legacy composition instead of naming their models/users return types. test/e2e/timetable mints its tokens through testpkg.MintTestJWT and arranges its template, exception and staffing rows through the fixture row types. Twelve keys fall (191 -> 179). No route, status code, error string, table or write owner changes. Outside the listed packages the cut changes only test files, as compile fixes for the new fixture return types: suites that update a fixture row through an owner repository read it back through that repository first, two packages that may import the owner models carry rows field for field (owner_rows_test.go, ownerDevice), and the repository suites that may not name models/schedule pass ISO literals or dates read back through the adapter. api/testutil re-exports the People Directory suite constructors as package variables, the shape careplan_contract.go already uses; their models/users result types stay behind the legacy composition key (#2747). Closing cut: every listed key is absent (the last three fell with #4001, #4014 and #4005), so the one policy rule still citing #2748, the compatibility permission test-support.e2e-test.inbound-parent-http, is deleted instead of converted to exact debt. The calendar end-to-end suite mounts the guardian portal through api.CalendarTestModule.ParentCalendarRouter, a root test hook beside newCareScheduleTestRouter that builds the portal resource with only the module's calendar wired, and no longer imports modules/careplan/inbound/parent. api already imports that package (root-composition.to.inbound-parent-http, #2750), so no key is introduced. No route, status code, error string, table or write owner changes.

The remaining 21 keys of #2748 do not fall without a decision. Most of them do not fall with a carrier either: they name implementation roles their owners keep, so they fall when the fixtures move to owner test support or reach owner contracts (#3944, ADR 0047); only the legacy composition services (#2747, #2751) and possibly modules/identityaccess/legacy/jwt (#3487) are dissolved by a carrier.
